To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a 3D model of the nucleus can be built from confocal microscopy data, (2) the 3D model can be used to study the spatial distribution of a nuclear compartment, (3) the spatial distribution is heterogeneous and depends on the cell type, (4) the spatial organization of the nuclear compartments is similar in animal and plant cells, and (5) the spatial distribution of the nuclear compartment is correlated with the distribution of nuclear pores.
the 3D nuclear organization in animal and plant cells is organized around the nucleolus, and the nucleolus is the main topological reference point for the organization of the rest of the nucleoplasm.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) to identify the nuclear compartment of interest in animal and plant cells; (2) to characterize its spatial distribution in 3D; (3) to model its organization in terms of spatial distribution and 3D structure; and (4) to compare animal and plant kingdoms in order to identify conserved principles and/or differences.
